title: Agent Cost Alert per Window
dataSources: Built-in Cost metric computed by Splunk Agent Observability from the traces in the Agent Stream; no evaluator is needed
description: Notifies the owning team when an Agent Stream's model spend in a window passes the agreed budget, using the built-in Cost alert in Splunk Agent Observability.
value: A loop that keeps calling the model, or a switch to a pricier model, can multiply spend within hours. A cost alert catches it before the invoice does.
implementation: On the Agent Stream's Alerts tab, add a Cost alert with aggregation sum, a threshold set from the stream's normal range, and a window. Route it to the owning team by email, Slack incoming webhook or generic HTTP webhook.
visualization: Alerts tab history for the stream; Cost over time in the console.
knownFalsePositives: Cost reads the Model Pricing table. A price change applies to new traces only, so the alert's level shifts at the change. The documentation does not say what a model missing from the table displays, so check Model Pricing before trusting the alert.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open the Agent Stream, go to the Alerts tab and add an alert. Each alert is an evaluator or a built-in metric (Status Code, Cost, Latency, Trace Count), an aggregation (average, min, max, count or sum), a threshold and a window. Notifications go to email, a Slack incoming webhook or a generic HTTP webhook. Alerts never block a request. A generic HTTP webhook receives a body with `event` (`alert.triggered`), `conditions[].observed_value`, `dedup_key`, `deep_link` and any `metadata` configured on the webhook. Webhook auth is none, bearer or HTTP basic, and the credential is write-only after save.

Step 3 — Validate

Check that the stream's models appear in Model Pricing, then confirm the per-trace cost on a few traces before trusting the alert. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Write the threshold and window into the team's runbook next to the alert, and review them after the first month of alerts. Use the `deep_link` in the notification to open the traces behind it.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Cost shows 0.0: check that the `model` string on the LLM spans has a row in Model Pricing, and report token counts until an admin adds it. Evaluator spend is on the separate Integration Costs page and is not in this alert.
grandmaExplanation: We add up what the assistant spends on each answer and get a message when it goes over budget.

productArtifacts.title: Cost alert on the Agent Stream
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Alerts tab > add alert
Metric: Cost
Aggregation: sum
Condition: Summed per-trace cost above the agreed budget for the window
Window: match the team's response time; a shorter window alerts sooner and is noisier
Notification: email, Slack incoming webhook, or generic HTTP webhook
Notes: Cost comes from token counts on LLM spans times the org Model Pricing table (UC-13.8.35).
